# Advanced Measurement Tool: tools for AI assistants

<!-- Generated by tools/export-tool-reference.mjs from the running plugin. Do not edit by hand. -->

32 tools, served by the `amt` MCP server 1.1.0 inside the Unreal Editor. An assistant reads the same list from the server itself (`tools/list`); this file is for people.

- Endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:47910/mcp` (or the next free port up to 47919). Run `AMT.Mcp` in the Output Log for the URL, the token and the connect command.
- The same tools run from the console: `AMT.Tools` lists them, `AMT.Tool <name> {json}` calls one; and from Blueprint or Python through `AMTMcpLibrary`.
- Names are `family_verb`; arguments are camelCase. An answer is a short sentence plus structured JSON; a refusal says what to do instead.

## What the server tells the assistant

```text
Advanced Measurement Tool (AMT) measures things in the open Unreal level: actors, regions, volumes, rooms. These tools drive it.
Begin with amt_status. To measure something the user names, turn the name into an actor id with scene_find_actors (or scene_get_selection for "this"), then measure_actor, measure_between, measure_region (a group of actors, a brush volume or a box) or measure_room (finds the room around a point by raycasting). measure_points computes any type from explicit points. These only answer unless you pass save=true, which also keeps the result as a measurement the viewport draws.
To dimension things for the user, use dimension_auto: it adds length, width and height dimension lines around each actor and keeps them linked, so dimension_refresh updates them after the actors move. measurement_list / _get / _update / _delete / _export / _import manage what is stored.
Show your work: viewport_show makes the viewport draw the measurements, viewport_focus frames actors, and viewport_screenshot returns the viewport as an image you can look at. Check a dimension against the picture before telling the user it is right.
Numbers come in base units: cm, cm2, cm3, degrees (each with a `text` in the user's own unit system, set by settings_get / settings_set). Quote `text` to the user. Tools marked as changing something add or edit measurements and can be undone with Ctrl+Z; confirm with the user before measurement_clear or any tool that deletes.
```

## status

### amt_status

**Advanced Measurement Tool status**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Start here. Says which Unreal project and level this editor has open, whether a Play-In-Editor session is running, the engine version, and which tool families Advanced Measurement Tool offers (the part of a tool's name before its first underscore). Read tools/list for the tools themselves.

No arguments.

## dimension

### dimension_auto

**Auto-dimension actors**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Dimensions actors for the user: around each actor's bounding box it adds a length (X), width (Y) and height (Z) dimension line, offset clear of the geometry, and the viewport shows them. Name the actors with `actors` (ids from scene_find_actors), or with the same filters scene_find_actors takes (`tag`, `folder`, `className`, `layer`, `query`, `minZ`/`maxZ`...; up to 100 actors per call), or select actors in the level. By default the box follows each actor's own axes (oriented=false uses the world's). Dimensions stay linked to their actor: dimension_refresh updates them after the actor moves or scales. Calling it again for the same actors replaces their earlier dimensions. One undo step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array of string |  | Actor ids, names or labels; empty = the actors the filters below name, or the selection. |
| `query` | string |  | Part of the actor's label or name. |
| `className` | string |  | Class name, or a parent class: StaticMeshActor, Volume. |
| `tag` | string |  | An actor tag. |
| `tags` | array of string |  | Several tags: the actor must carry all of them (anyTag: any one). |
| `anyTag` | boolean |  | With `tags`: match actors that carry any of them, not all. |
| `folder` | string |  | An outliner folder, e.g. "Building/Walls": the folder and everything under it. |
| `layer` | string |  | A layer the actor is in. |
| `selected` | boolean |  | Only actors selected in the editor. |
| `minZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle (the centre of their bounding box) is at least this high, in cm: the bottom of a floor. |
| `maxZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle is lower than this, in cm: the top of a floor. With minZ, one storey of a building. |
| `axes` | array of string |  | Which of length, width, height (default all three). |
| `oriented` | boolean |  | Along each actor's own axes (default true) or the world's. |
| `offsetCm` | number |  | How far the dimension lines sit outside the box, in cm (default: 8% of the actor's largest side, 15-120). |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Replace earlier auto dimensions of the same actors (default true). |
| `color` | string or array |  | "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1; default the settings' line colour. |
| `show` | boolean |  | Make the viewport draw measurements now (default true). |

### dimension_clear

**Remove auto dimensions**. **Destructive**: removes data; the assistant should ask you first.

Removes the dimensions dimension_auto made: one actor's (`actor`), the stale ones whose actor was deleted (`staleOnly`), or all of them (`all`). Measurements the user made by hand are never touched. Undoable. Confirm with the user before `all`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string |  | Remove this actor's dimensions. |
| `staleOnly` | boolean |  | Remove only dimensions whose actor no longer exists. |
| `all` | boolean |  | Remove every auto dimension. |

### dimension_refresh

**Refresh dimensions**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Recomputes the auto dimensions from their actors' current size and place, after the actors were moved, rotated or scaled. Dimensions whose actor is gone are marked stale. Optionally only one actor's.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string |  | Only this actor's dimensions. |

## measure

### measure_actor

**Measure an actor**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Measures one actor: its length (X), width (Y) and height (Z) along its own axes (or the world's with oriented=false), its world bounds, and its bounding-box footprint and volume. With mesh=true also the real surface area, enclosed volume (only for a closed mesh) and convex footprint area, read from the static mesh triangles. Numbers are in cm, cm2, cm3, each with `text` in the user's unit system. Does not change the level.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string | yes | Actor id, name or label (from scene_find_actors). |
| `oriented` | boolean |  | Measure along the actor's own axes (default true) or the world's. |
| `mesh` | boolean |  | Also measure the mesh: surface area, volume, footprint (default false). |
| `onlyColliding` | boolean |  | Count only components with collision. |

### measure_actors

**Measure many actors**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Measures a group of actors in one call: for each its length (X), width (Y) and height (Z) along its own axes, its bounding-box volume and footprint, with totals and a summary by class. Name the actors with `actors` (ids), or with the filters scene_find_actors takes (`tag`, `folder`, `className`, `layer`, `query`, `minZ`/`maxZ` for one storey...; up to 200 actors per call), or select them in the level. Use it for "the size of every wall on the second floor". Does not change the level; measurement_from_actors and dimension_auto add measurements.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array of string |  | Actor ids, names or labels; empty = the actors the filters below name, or the selection. |
| `query` | string |  | Part of the actor's label or name. |
| `className` | string |  | Class name, or a parent class: StaticMeshActor, Volume. |
| `tag` | string |  | An actor tag. |
| `tags` | array of string |  | Several tags: the actor must carry all of them (anyTag: any one). |
| `anyTag` | boolean |  | With `tags`: match actors that carry any of them, not all. |
| `folder` | string |  | An outliner folder, e.g. "Building/Walls": the folder and everything under it. |
| `layer` | string |  | A layer the actor is in. |
| `selected` | boolean |  | Only actors selected in the editor. |
| `minZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle (the centre of their bounding box) is at least this high, in cm: the bottom of a floor. |
| `maxZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle is lower than this, in cm: the top of a floor. With minZ, one storey of a building. |
| `oriented` | boolean |  | Measure along each actor's own axes (default true) or the world's. |
| `mesh` | boolean |  | Also measure each mesh: surface area and, for a closed mesh, volume (at most 50 actors). |
| `onlyColliding` | boolean |  | Count only components with collision. |
| `sortBy` | string: `label` / `length` / `width` / `height` / `volume` / `footprint` |  | Order the list by length, width, height, volume or footprint (default: by label). |
| `descending` | boolean |  | With sortBy: largest first (default true). |

### measure_between

**Measure the distance between two things**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

The distance between two actors or points: straight, horizontal and vertical. Each end is an actor id or a point [x, y, z] in cm. mode=nearest gives the clear gap between two actors' bounding boxes (clearance, spacing); the default is centre to centre. Set save=true to keep it as a distance measurement the viewport draws.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string or array | yes | An actor id, or a point [x, y, z] in cm. |
| `to` | string or array | yes | An actor id, or a point [x, y, z] in cm. |
| `mode` | string: `center` / `nearest` |  | center: centre to centre (default). nearest: the gap between the two actors' bounding boxes (0 when they touch). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Also keep the result as a measurement in the level, so the viewport shows it (default false: only answer). |
| `label` | string |  | A title for the saved measurement, e.g. "Length". |
| `color` | string or array |  | Colour of the saved measurement: "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

### measure_points

**Measure from points**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Computes any measurement type from explicit points, exactly as the viewport tools do: Distance, Angle (at the middle point), Area (any polygon, in 3D), Volume (box from two corners), Polyline (path length), Perimeter (closed loop), Radius (circle through three points, with its diameter) and Slope (degrees and percent). save=true keeps it as a measurement.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string: `Distance` / `Angle` / `Area` / `Volume` / `Polyline` / `Perimeter` / `Radius` / `Slope` | yes | The measurement type. |
| `points` | array of array | yes | The points in cm. Distance, Slope, Volume: 2 (Volume: opposite corners of a box). Angle: 3 (start, vertex, end). Radius: 3 points on the circle. Area, Perimeter: 3 or more. Polyline: 2 or more. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Also keep the result as a measurement in the level, so the viewport shows it (default false: only answer). |
| `label` | string |  | A title for the saved measurement, e.g. "Length". |
| `color` | string or array |  | Colour of the saved measurement: "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

### measure_raycast

**Cast a measuring ray**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Casts a ray from a point and reports what it hits: the distance, the hit point and surface normal, the surface slope (0 degrees = floor, 90 = wall) and the actor. Use it to probe clearances and wall distances. save=true keeps origin-to-hit as a distance measurement.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin` | array of number | yes | Where the ray starts, [x, y, z] in cm. |
| `direction` | array of number |  | The direction, [x, y, z] (any length). |
| `to` | array of number |  | Or a point to aim at. |
| `maxDistanceCm` | number |  | How far it looks, in cm (default 10000). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Also keep the result as a measurement in the level, so the viewport shows it (default false: only answer). |
| `label` | string |  | A title for the saved measurement, e.g. "Length". |
| `color` | string or array |  | Colour of the saved measurement: "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

### measure_region

**Measure a region**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Measures a region of the level given as ONE of: `actors` (the box around a group of actors, e.g. a whole building), `volume` (a brush volume actor, measured exactly) or `box` (explicit corners). Gives its length, width, height, bounding-box footprint and volume. save=true keeps the box as a volume measurement.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array of string |  | Actor ids (at most 200): the region is the box around all of them. |
| `volume` | string |  | A brush volume actor (trigger, blocking volume...): its exact brush volume and area are given. |
| `box` | object |  | An explicit box: {"min": [x,y,z], "max": [x,y,z]} in cm. |
| `mesh` | boolean |  | With actors: also add up their mesh surface, closed-mesh volume and footprint. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Also keep the result as a measurement in the level, so the viewport shows it (default false: only answer). |
| `label` | string |  | A title for the saved measurement, e.g. "Length". |
| `color` | string or array |  | Colour of the saved measurement: "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

### measure_room

**Detect and measure a room**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Finds the room around a point by casting a ring of rays against the level's collision, and measures it: floor area, perimeter, longest/shortest span, nearest wall, ceiling height and volume. It reports `enclosed`: false means rays escaped (open space), so the area is not a room. Geometry needs collision to be seen. The outline is reduced to the room's corners (a rectangular room is four points). save=true keeps that outline as an area measurement and the height as a distance, when the space is enclosed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `point` | array of number |  | A point inside the room, [x, y, z] in cm. |
| `actor` | string |  | Or an actor inside the room (the centre of its bounds is used). |
| `rays` | integer |  | Rays in the horizontal ring, 8-720 (default 72). |
| `maxDistanceCm` | number |  | How far a ray looks, in cm (default 3000). |
| `probeHeightCm` | number |  | Height above the floor the ring is cast at, in cm (default 120). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Also keep the result as a measurement in the level, so the viewport shows it (default false: only answer). |
| `label` | string |  | A title for the saved measurement, e.g. "Length". |
| `color` | string or array |  | Colour of the saved measurement: "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

## measurement

### measurement_clear

**Clear all measurements**. **Destructive**: removes data; the assistant should ask you first.

Removes every measurement in the level. Needs confirm=true, which you pass only after the user agreed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | yes | Must be true. |

### measurement_create

**Create a measurement**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Stores a measurement of any type through points you give (cm). The result and label are computed for you. Use the measure_* tools with save=true when the points come from actors or the scene.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string: `Distance` / `Angle` / `Area` / `Volume` / `Polyline` / `Perimeter` / `Radius` / `Slope` | yes | The measurement type. |
| `points` | array of array | yes | Points in cm; see measure_points for the count each type takes. |
| `title` | string |  | Shown instead of the type's name, e.g. "Door width". |
| `color` | string or array |  | "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |
| `show` | boolean |  | Make the viewport draw measurements now (default true). |

### measurement_delete

**Delete measurements**. **Destructive**: removes data; the assistant should ask you first.

Removes measurements by id (undoable with Ctrl+Z). Confirm with the user first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array of string | yes | Measurement ids. |

### measurement_export

**Export measurements**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Writes the measurements (all, or the `ids`) to a CSV or JSON file inside the project: a plain file name goes to Saved/AMT/Exports. Gives the path.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | string: `csv` / `json` |  | csv or json (default json). |
| `path` | string |  | A file name, or a path inside the project; default a timestamped name. |
| `ids` | array of string |  | Only these measurements. |

### measurement_from_actors

**Add a measurement to each actor**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Adds one area or volume measurement per actor (up to 100 per call), titled with the actor's label, kept in the level and drawn in the viewport. Name the actors like measure_actors does: `actors`, the filters, or the selection. For length, width and height dimensions use dimension_auto. Calling it again for the same actors replaces its earlier measurements. One undo step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string: `area` / `volume` | yes | area: the footprint of each actor's box. volume: the volume of its box (in world axes). |
| `actors` | array of string |  | Actor ids, names or labels; empty = the actors the filters below name, or the selection. |
| `query` | string |  | Part of the actor's label or name. |
| `className` | string |  | Class name, or a parent class: StaticMeshActor, Volume. |
| `tag` | string |  | An actor tag. |
| `tags` | array of string |  | Several tags: the actor must carry all of them (anyTag: any one). |
| `anyTag` | boolean |  | With `tags`: match actors that carry any of them, not all. |
| `folder` | string |  | An outliner folder, e.g. "Building/Walls": the folder and everything under it. |
| `layer` | string |  | A layer the actor is in. |
| `selected` | boolean |  | Only actors selected in the editor. |
| `minZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle (the centre of their bounding box) is at least this high, in cm: the bottom of a floor. |
| `maxZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle is lower than this, in cm: the top of a floor. With minZ, one storey of a building. |
| `color` | string or array |  | "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1; default the settings' line colour. |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Replace the earlier measurements this tool made for the same actors and kind (default true). |
| `show` | boolean |  | Make the viewport draw measurements now (default true). |

### measurement_get

**Get a measurement**. Reads only: never changes anything.

One measurement with its points.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The measurement id. |

### measurement_import

**Import measurements**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Reads measurements from a JSON file inside the project: an AMT export, or the autosave file. mode=merge (default) adds the ones not already there; mode=replace first clears the level's measurements and needs confirm=true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | A file name under Saved/AMT/Exports, or a path inside the project. |
| `mode` | string: `merge` / `replace` |  | merge (default) or replace. |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required true for mode=replace. |
| `show` | boolean |  | Make the viewport draw measurements now (default true). |

### measurement_list

**List measurements**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The measurements stored in the level, oldest first: id, type, label, `text` (in the user's units), value in base units (cm, cm2, cm3, degrees), title, colour and metadata. Filter by type, by the actor a dimension belongs to, or by source (mcp, mcp-dimension). Measurements the user made by hand have no source.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string: `Distance` / `Angle` / `Area` / `Volume` / `Polyline` / `Perimeter` / `Radius` / `Slope` |  | Only this type. |
| `actor` | string |  | Only dimensions of this actor. |
| `source` | string |  | Only this source: mcp, mcp-dimension. |
| `withPoints` | boolean |  | Include each measurement's points. |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many (default 100, up to 500). |
| `offset` | integer |  | Skip this many first. |

### measurement_update

**Edit a measurement**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Changes a measurement's points, title or colour; the result and label are recomputed. Editing the points of an auto dimension unlinks it from its actor.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The measurement id. |
| `points` | array of array |  | New points in cm. |
| `title` | string |  | New title; empty removes it. |
| `color` | string or array |  | "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. |

## scene

### scene_find_actors

**Find actors**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Finds actors in the open level by what the outliner shows and says where they are. Filter by `query` (part of the label or name), `className` (a class or any parent, e.g. StaticMeshActor), `tag` or `tags`, `folder` (an outliner folder and everything under it), `layer`, `selected`, or one storey of a building with `minZ` and `maxZ` (the height of the actor's middle, in cm). All the conditions given must hold. Each actor has an `id` that every other tool takes as `actor`, and its folder and tags. Start with scene_outline to see what the level contains, then use this to turn what the user calls an object ("the north wall", "the doors on the second floor") into ids.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string |  | Part of the actor's label or name. |
| `className` | string |  | Class name, or a parent class: StaticMeshActor, Volume. |
| `tag` | string |  | An actor tag. |
| `tags` | array of string |  | Several tags: the actor must carry all of them (anyTag: any one). |
| `anyTag` | boolean |  | With `tags`: match actors that carry any of them, not all. |
| `folder` | string |  | An outliner folder, e.g. "Building/Walls": the folder and everything under it. |
| `layer` | string |  | A layer the actor is in. |
| `selected` | boolean |  | Only actors selected in the editor. |
| `minZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle (the centre of their bounding box) is at least this high, in cm: the bottom of a floor. |
| `maxZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle is lower than this, in cm: the top of a floor. With minZ, one storey of a building. |
| `withBounds` | boolean |  | Include each actor's bounding box. |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many (default 50, up to 500). |
| `offset` | integer |  | Skip this many first, to page through a long answer. |

### scene_get_actor

**Describe an actor**. Reads only: never changes anything.

One actor in detail: class, folder, tags, bounds, its size along its own axes (length, width, height) and its mesh components with triangle counts.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string | yes | Actor id, name or label. |

### scene_get_selection

**Get the selection**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The actors the user has selected in the level, with their bounds. Use it when the user says "measure this" or "the selected ones".

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `withBounds` | boolean |  | Include each actor's bounding box (default true). |

### scene_outline

**Outline the level**. Reads only: never changes anything.

What the level contains, as the outliner shows it: how many actors, the folders (each with the lowest and highest point of what is in it, so a storey can be matched to a folder or to a height band), and the tags, classes and layers with how many actors carry each. Takes the same filters as scene_find_actors to outline only a part. Use it first when the user names a group ("the walls of the office building", "the second floor") and you do not yet know what the level calls it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string |  | Part of the actor's label or name. |
| `className` | string |  | Class name, or a parent class: StaticMeshActor, Volume. |
| `tag` | string |  | An actor tag. |
| `tags` | array of string |  | Several tags: the actor must carry all of them (anyTag: any one). |
| `anyTag` | boolean |  | With `tags`: match actors that carry any of them, not all. |
| `folder` | string |  | An outliner folder, e.g. "Building/Walls": the folder and everything under it. |
| `layer` | string |  | A layer the actor is in. |
| `selected` | boolean |  | Only actors selected in the editor. |
| `minZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle (the centre of their bounding box) is at least this high, in cm: the bottom of a floor. |
| `maxZ` | number |  | Only actors whose middle is lower than this, in cm: the top of a floor. With minZ, one storey of a building. |
| `top` | integer |  | At most this many entries in each list (default 40, up to 200). |

### scene_select

**Select actors**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Selects actors in the level so the user sees what you mean. Replaces the selection unless `add` is true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array of string | yes | Actor ids, names or labels. |
| `add` | boolean |  | Add to the selection instead of replacing it. |

## settings

### settings_get

**Get the AMT settings**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The Advanced Measurement Tool settings that decide how measurements are shown and in which units: measurementUnit (Metric or Imperial), angleUnit, areaUnit, volumeUnit, line colour and thickness, point size, text scale, always-on-top, projection lines, snapping.

No arguments.

### settings_reset

**Restore the AMT settings**. **Destructive**: removes data; the assistant should ask you first.

Puts every Advanced Measurement Tool setting back to the value the plugin ships with (units, line colour and thickness, snapping...). This is the same as the dashboard's Restore Defaults button. It overwrites the user's own choices, so ask first.

No arguments.

### settings_set

**Change the AMT settings**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Changes settings by name, e.g. {"measurementUnit": "Imperial", "lineThickness": 3, "lineColor": {"r": 1, "g": 0.4, "b": 0, "a": 1}}. Names are those settings_get returns; values outside a setting's range are refused. The change is saved to the project's editor settings and the viewport redraws. Ask the user before changing units.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changes` | object | yes | The settings to change, name to value. |

## viewport

### viewport_camera

**Get or set the viewport camera**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Reads the level viewport camera (location in cm, rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees), or moves it: `location`, then `lookAt` (a point to face) or `rotation`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | array of number |  | Camera location [x, y, z] in cm. |
| `lookAt` | array of number |  | A point the camera faces. |
| `rotation` | array of number |  | [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees (ignored when lookAt is given). |

### viewport_focus

**Frame things in the viewport**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Moves the level viewport camera to frame actors, one measurement, or a box. Use it before viewport_screenshot so the picture shows what you want to check.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array of string |  | Actor ids to frame. |
| `measurement` | string |  | A measurement id to frame. |
| `box` | object |  | {"min": [x,y,z], "max": [x,y,z]} in cm. |

### viewport_screenshot

**Take a viewport screenshot**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Returns the level viewport as a PNG image you can look at: use it to check that dimensions sit where you meant, and that the right actors were measured. Call viewport_show first so measurements are drawn, and viewport_focus to frame the subject. Needs the viewport tab to be visible in the editor.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxWidth` | integer |  | Scale down to at most this width in pixels (default 1280, 256-3840). |

### viewport_show

**Show measurements in the viewport**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Makes the level viewport draw the stored measurements (dimension lines, outlines, labels): it switches the Advanced Measurement Tool mode on. With no tool picked the mode takes no input. visible=false switches it off. The measure_* tools with save=true and dimension_auto call this themselves.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | boolean |  | true (default) shows, false hides. |
